Arthur Penny was the first in sight, with a very substantial lead, with Cohen after him, slowly decreasing the lead and, wonder of wonders, Penny even had energy enough to run wide at the last turn (or perhaps he couldn't see) but anyway, Cohen did the same.

The start was a good one in which Cohen (Ashcombe A.C.), Joe Flower and Dewberry showed to advantage, then over half a mile of parkland and encircling the Deer Enclosure with the runners in the following order: Cohen, Allum, Penny, Jack Flower, Frank Webb, Nuti (T.V.H.), Carter, Dewberry, Morrell, R…
After completing a circle round the starting field the leading positions were held by Belton (Surrey A.C.), Cohen (Ashcombe A.C.), Penny, Cook, Stansbury (Ranelagh), and Wills.

Arthur Penny had a fine fight with Cohen, of Ashcombe, while Vic Harman, of Slough, found the pace a little too hot for him. Bert Footer ran his usual dogged race, while our Captain, Bill Webb, just strode round enjoying the beauty of this pleasantly-situated track.

Going out towards the village, Cohen of Ashcombe crept up and took the lead when crossing the Golf Links. The runners were now beginning to thin out, but T.V.H. had a good crowd of their men with ours at this point.

The Two miles team race gave us an easy win, although every credit is due to Cohen, of Ashcombe, for his fine individual victory. The Medley relay race also came our way; and so once again the Shield is in Belgravian possession, where we shall try to keep it.
Cohen finished first for Ashcombe, filling the 13th position, and Phipps, the first T.V.H. man, being 9th. Our sealed handicap held in conjuction proved to be an all-junior affair.
When seen at the end of about a mile and a half the field was led by Close (Reading) followed by a bunch including Cohen (Ashcombe) and Pell (Herne Hill).

Parker, Penny and Cohen finished equal first, closely followed by Shaw, Williams and Verney. We were obviously much too strong for our University friends, who lacked the assistance of Etheridge; but, nevertheless, the sporting match was greatly enjoyed by all.

Ten of our points were amassed in the one and two mile events through the events of Cohen, Carter, Shields and Taylor. Our remaining points came from Lee (440 yards), and Quackenbos and Grassau (High Jump).

A small bunch of four runners gradually left the rest of the field, these being Carter, Penny, Cohen and Allum. It soon became a question of who would crack first; and Allum was seen to be slowly falling behind.

After a fairly fast start, Les Cohen was in the lead at the Brook, but Art Penny was closing on him, and a Thames Valley man was in third position.
As is usual the cracks set the pace, Penny, Cohen (who is showing improved form this year) leading, Ring, Taylor, Stimpson and Parker being bunched just behind.

Penny was next, followed by Carter, Cohen, Ring, and Wood (who won the Surrey Junior Race the week after) in the first twenty places. Our hopes of repeating our win of last year were now very bright; and we next saw the field coming round Tattenham Corner led by Bert Footer, followed by Belton.
From the very start Pat Parker looked the winner and after the first mile he was leading, but followed very closely by Carter, Cohen, Stimpson and Ring, with the rest of the field in hot pursuit.
Les Cohen now carried our colours from Merstham to Earlswood Common. The lead was increased to one of 25 seconds over Birchfield, with Mitcham still in the third place.
We then saw Les Cohen, Tom Carter, and Arthur Penny move away from the rest; although Dan Patience was running well close behind. In the last lap a hectic struggle ensued.
As usual, the Mile provided the spectators with an exciting race, and a field of 18 faced the starter. Les Cohen soon showed that he was determined to keep in front; but W.
The 1 Mile team race provided the large crowd with a big thrill; Les Cohen and Thorogood, the A.A.A. Indoor 2 Mile Champion, having a ding-dong battle over the last 200 yds.

Jimmy Kemp, evidently feeling robust, was soon up in the front, together with Les Cohen, and they kept in the lead most of the way. Nearing home Penny and Footer came along and with Cohen going slightly off the trail, these two and Kemp eventually came home together.

The holder, Les Cohen, was among the starters who were quite numerous, although Pat Parker, owing to his domicile, was an absentee. The first mile was reached in 5 min. 2 sec., the second in 10 min. 14 sec., and the leading bunch included all the Club’s most prominent distance runners.

Percy Bicknell, of the Valley, was the individual winner, followed by Cohen (Ashcombe) and Mick Pyer (Belgrave). Three weeks later a similar fixture was held at Wimbledon over a five miles course, and ninety runners finished.
Our team was not so strong as in former years, owing to the absence of Footer and Cohen, but we had hopes of at least repeating our performance of last year in finishing second to Mitcham.

Herbert's reserve pace gave him a good win, but the form shewn by all our runners inspires confidence in their ability to win the "News of the World" event at the end of the month. Handicap: 1, Smart; 2, Cohen; 3, Stimpson.
In the mile, Bill Lucas had a grand tussle with Bingham, T.C.C., who won by a few yards in 4m 32 secs., Cohen finishing 3rd. In the field events, Sutton and Jones upheld the club's prestige.
